chapters.title: Out of Africa
chapters.tease: One species from one continent became the only human on every continent but Antarctica.

chapters.title: The Cognitive Spark
chapters.tease: Symbols let humans trust strangers, and that made very large groups possible.

chapters.title: Fire and the Brain
chapters.tease: Cooking let our ancestors spend less energy on their guts and more on their brains.

chapters.title: The First Artists
chapters.tease: Long before writing, people used images to record, to teach and to wonder.

chapters.title: The Farming Bargain
chapters.tease: Farming won not because it made lives better, but because it fed more people.

chapters.title: Domesticating Life
chapters.tease: In reshaping plants and animals, humans reshaped their own lives and even their genes.

chapters.title: The First Towns
chapters.tease: Thousands of people lived side by side for centuries without palaces or kings.

chapters.title: The Surplus Trap
chapters.tease: Whoever controlled the granary soon controlled the people who filled it.

chapters.title: Marks Become Words
chapters.tease: Writing was invented by accountants. Poets and lawmakers came later.

chapters.title: Settling Changed Us
chapters.tease: Staying put made civilisation possible, and made its costs unavoidable.

chapters.title: The Land Between Rivers
chapters.tease: The first cities, scripts and law codes were invented here, on a hard, flood-prone plain.

chapters.title: The Gift of the Nile
chapters.tease: A river that rose on time made a state that outlasted every other in the ancient world.

chapters.title: The Indus Enigma
chapters.tease: The largest of the first civilisations left superb cities and a writing system nobody can read.

chapters.title: The Mandate of Heaven
chapters.tease: It made power conditional on good government, and gave every rebel a ready-made justification.

chapters.title: Hammurabi's Code
chapters.tease: It made rules public and fixed, even as it wrote inequality of rank straight into the law.

chapters.title: The Wheel and Sail
chapters.tease: Moving grain, goods and armies cheaply was the hidden precondition of every early state.

chapters.title: Cities of Gods
chapters.tease: The tallest building in the first cities belonged to a god, and so, in a sense, did the city.

chapters.title: Bronze Age Collapse
chapters.tease: The first globalised system showed how linked economies can fall together rather than one by one.

chapters.title: The Alphabet Spreads
chapters.tease: One sign per sound made writing learnable in weeks, and seeded most of the world's scripts.

chapters.title: Writing Outlives Empire
chapters.tease: Dynasties were scaffolding; the ideas they sheltered became the inheritance of everyone.

chapters.title: The Axial Age
chapters.tease: Four regions, barely in contact, framed moral questions that religion and philosophy still ask.

chapters.title: Athens Tries Democracy
chapters.tease: The best-documented early attempt to let ordinary citizens govern directly, by vote and by lot.

chapters.title: The Persian Superpower
chapters.tease: The first state built to run a truly multi-ethnic world, and a template for empires after it.

chapters.title: Alexander's Fusion
chapters.tease: A war of conquest became the start of a shared culture stretching from Sicily to Afghanistan.

chapters.title: The Roman Republic
chapters.tease: A government designed to stop any one man ruling, whose machinery modern republics copied.

chapters.title: Roads, Law, Concrete
chapters.tease: Engineering and administration, not just the legions, made Roman rule last.

chapters.title: The Han Mirror
chapters.tease: A rival model of empire, built on educated officials, that China rebuilt again and again.

chapters.title: Empire Buys Peace
chapters.tease: Proof that peace under empire can be real, and a reminder of who pays for it.

chapters.title: Why Rome Fell
chapters.tease: The classic case of slow decline: many wounds, each making the others worse.

chapters.title: The Classical Debt
chapters.tease: Much of how the modern world argues about power was first argued in Athens and Rome.

chapters.title: One God Rising
chapters.tease: A small, often conquered people exported the most influential religious idea of the ancient world.

chapters.title: Christianity Goes Global
chapters.tease: The empire that crucified Jesus ended up carrying his symbol on its banners.

chapters.title: The Rise of Islam
chapters.tease: A new faith united Arabia's tribes and, within a century, ruled from the Atlantic to the Indus.

chapters.title: The House of Wisdom
chapters.tease: Much of what Europe later called Greek learning arrived through Arabic, and returned improved.

chapters.title: Byzantium Endures
chapters.tease: The half of Rome most people forget kept law, faith and Greek learning alive for a thousand years.

chapters.title: The Buddhist Road
chapters.tease: An idea crossed a continent with no army behind it, carried by monks, translators and caravans.

chapters.title: Charlemagne's Europe
chapters.tease: A Christmas coronation in 800 planted the idea of a single Christian Europe under one crown.

chapters.title: Faith Builds Wonders
chapters.tease: What a society builds shows what it values, and for a thousand years it built for heaven.

chapters.title: The Crusades Collide
chapters.tease: The crusaders set out to win a city and ended up reconnecting a sea.

chapters.title: Belief Moves History
chapters.tease: For a millennium, religion set the clocks, wrote the laws, ran the schools and drew the maps.

chapters.title: The Silk Roads
chapters.tease: A relay of strangers linked Han China and Rome, and moved faiths and germs as well as silk.

chapters.title: The Mongol Peace
chapters.tease: A brutal conquest created a century of safe roads, open trade and travelling ideas across Eurasia.

chapters.title: Mansa Musa's Gold
chapters.tease: One pilgrimage revealed to the Mediterranean world where much of its gold came from.

chapters.title: The Indian Ocean
chapters.tease: The richest trade network on Earth ran on a seasonal wind, and Europe joined it late.

chapters.title: The Black Death
chapters.tease: Mass death made labour scarce, and scarce labour gave survivors the power to refuse serfdom.

chapters.title: Cahokia and the Maya
chapters.tease: Pyramids rose on both sides of an ocean no one had crossed, proof that civilisation is a human pattern.

chapters.title: Paper and Powder
chapters.tease: The tools that made the modern West, from books to cannon, were largely borrowed from China.

chapters.title: Timbuktu's Libraries
chapters.tease: Gold and salt paid for a city of books, a written African scholarship that has survived to this day.

chapters.title: Ideas Ride With Goods
chapters.tease: Every caravan carried an invisible cargo of ideas and germs that changed worlds more than its goods.

chapters.title: The Connected Old World
chapters.tease: The world was already global by 1400, and its centre lay in China and the Islamic lands, not in Europe.

chapters.title: The Renaissance Turn
chapters.tease: Looking back to Rome and Greece gave ambitious Italians a new standard, set outside the Church.

chapters.title: Gutenberg's Press
chapters.tease: Print broke the scribes' monopoly on copying and turned knowledge into a mass-produced good.

chapters.title: Leonardo's Mind
chapters.tease: He made close observation a method, filling thousands of pages with questions about how things work.

chapters.title: The Reformation Splits
chapters.tease: One church became many, and religion became a matter of states, wars and individual conscience.

chapters.title: The Ming Voyages
chapters.tease: The world's largest fleet reached Africa, then was recalled, leaving the sea lanes to others.

chapters.title: Banking Powers Art
chapters.tease: Credit paid for beauty: banking profits bought churches, frescoes and the favour of popes.

chapters.title: A New Sky
chapters.tease: Setting the Earth in motion moved humanity off the centre and opened the Scientific Revolution.

chapters.title: Humanism's Wager
chapters.tease: Humanism put eloquence, evidence and human worth at the heart of European education.

chapters.title: Ideas Become Cheap
chapters.tease: Censors could ban books, but not the presses beyond their borders; dissent became impossible to stamp out.

chapters.title: The West Wakes Up
chapters.tease: Europe was not yet the richest region, but it was restless, divided and armed with print.

chapters.title: 1492 Changes Everything
chapters.tease: Two hemispheres that had developed apart for over ten thousand years were joined for good.

chapters.title: The Columbian Exchange
chapters.tease: The biggest reshuffle of living things since the continents drifted apart rewrote every kitchen on Earth.

chapters.title: The Great Dying
chapters.tease: The largest population collapse in recorded history, and most of it was done by microbes.

chapters.title: Silver Circles the Globe
chapters.tease: A mountain in the Andes and a tax reform in Beijing created the first truly global market.

chapters.title: The Atlantic Slave Trade
chapters.tease: The largest forced migration in history built the plantation wealth of the Atlantic world.

chapters.title: Gunpowder Empires
chapters.tease: While Europe fought itself, three Muslim empires ruled the richest lands between the Danube and the Ganges.

chapters.title: The Ottoman Bridge
chapters.tease: One dynasty held the hinge of three continents for over six hundred years.

chapters.title: Companies Rule Nations
chapters.tease: Shareholders in two northern ports came to rule millions of people in Asia.

chapters.title: The Little Ice Age
chapters.tease: The seventeenth century's wars and fallen dynasties often began with a failed harvest.

chapters.title: One World, Unequally
chapters.tease: Globalisation and inequality were born together, and they grew up side by side.

chapters.title: The Scientific Method
chapters.tease: It turned knowledge from something inherited into something tested, and so endlessly improvable.

chapters.title: The Enlightenment
chapters.tease: It supplied the language of rights and consent that modern constitutions still speak.

chapters.title: The Steam Engine
chapters.tease: For the first time, work came from a fuel that never tired, so output could compound.

chapters.title: The Great Divergence
chapters.tease: It explains how a few small countries came to dominate the globe for two centuries.

chapters.title: The American Experiment
chapters.tease: It made a written constitution, not a royal bloodline, the source of a nation's authority.

chapters.title: The French Revolution
chapters.tease: It invented modern left and right, and showed that revolution can free and consume at once.

chapters.title: The Haitian Revolution
chapters.tease: It was the only revolution of its age to end slavery by force and keep it ended.

chapters.title: Nations Are Invented
chapters.tease: It became the world's default answer to the question of who should rule whom.

chapters.title: The Factory World
chapters.tease: It created both modern prosperity and modern protest, often in the same street.

chapters.title: Ideas Overthrow Kings
chapters.tease: Authority moved from birth and tradition to argument, evidence and consent.

chapters.title: The First World War
chapters.tease: Machine guns, artillery and railways met nineteenth-century diplomacy, and the old order did not survive.

chapters.title: The Russian Revolution
chapters.tease: A promise of peace, land and bread became a one-party state that shaped the whole twentieth century.

chapters.title: The Great Depression
chapters.tease: Mass unemployment shook faith in markets and democracy, and opened the door to dictators.

chapters.title: The Second World War
chapters.tease: It showed what industrial states could do when they set out to conquer and exterminate.

chapters.title: The Nuclear Age
chapters.tease: For the first time, a species gained the means to end its own civilisation in an afternoon.

chapters.title: The End of Empire
chapters.tease: In thirty years, empires built over four centuries gave way to dozens of new nations.

chapters.title: The Cold War
chapters.tease: Two superpowers divided the planet into camps and turned every region into a board for their contest.

chapters.title: The Rights Revolutions
chapters.tease: Within living memory, most of humanity gained rights once kept for a privileged few.

chapters.title: The Great Acceleration
chapters.tease: In one lifetime, human activity became a force on the scale of geology.

chapters.title: The Century That Broke
chapters.tease: The same discoveries that fed and healed billions also killed tens of millions.

chapters.title: The Digital Turn
chapters.tease: It turned all information into cheap, copyable code and wired the world into one network.

chapters.title: Everyone Connected
chapters.tease: For the first time, nearly any human could reach almost any other in seconds.

chapters.title: The Genome Read
chapters.tease: Reading and rewriting DNA gave humans power over heredity itself.

chapters.title: The Climate Reckoning
chapters.tease: Humanity's greatest test is acting on a danger that unfolds over decades, not election cycles.

chapters.title: The Rise of AI
chapters.tease: A tool that extends thinking itself could transform every field that depends on it.

chapters.title: The Global Village
chapters.tease: Interdependence meant that a single event in one city could reach every continent within weeks.

chapters.title: The New Great Powers
chapters.tease: The West's lead now looks like a two-century interlude rather than the natural order.

chapters.title: Longer, Richer Lives
chapters.tease: Ordinary people now live longer, healthier lives than kings and emperors could once expect.

chapters.title: Our Fragile Powers
chapters.tease: Humanity's new powers are growing faster than the rules and institutions meant to steer them.

chapters.title: History Isn't Over
chapters.tease: Every 'permanent' order in this book ended, and every future turned on choices people made.
